findings.summary: Keep template visibility explicit for both shared closures and sprite atlas helpers.
Render standalone and shared data preambles in one traversal.
Remove redundant source and declaration fields from emitted-definition records.
Skip identifier scanning for units without generated templates and retain only template dependencies.
Reuse extensionless source path stems for C++ filenames and worker directories.
Remove count assertions already covered by exact generated path assertions.
Reuse temporary-binding logic for constructed method receivers.
Keep fresh string results directly initialized; snapshot only borrowed expressions.
Skip bodyless callees before computing traversal keys or memoizing them.
Reuse resolved call expressions and flatten callback-binding traversal.
Copy callback environments only when binding callback parameters.
Skip handle classification once method sharing is established.
Centralize concrete and template body registration for shared functions, closures and coroutines.
Remove obsolete static expansion work accounting while retaining traversal safety proofs.
Cache scalar-fold metadata by specialization without caching or skipping runtime calls.
Render each concrete capture environment type once.
Remove the redundant wrapper around shared-call lowering.
Use typed declarations to preserve actual optional, tuple and texture capture storage.
Keep UI metadata inspection in a rolled-back emission transaction.
Propagate declared parameter constness through native reference aliases.
Reuse record snapshot invalidation for mutable native and shared-call arguments.
Mark source bindings consistently when generation metadata can consume their uses.
Borrow immutable string results through the existing stable-binding proof.
Reuse pinned RHS ownership across destructuring writes instead of copying stable results.
Register owned callback arguments before binding their source aliases.
Use explicit compile-time bindings for texture-list composition.
